articles.body: As of November 2026. You need Power BI Desktop, a Power BI account and a Windows machine for the on-premises data gateway. Last week Claude built a Power BI report on 182 million flights in ClickHouse . It ran in Power BI Desktop. The next question is the one every BI team asks: can the rest of the team open it in the Power BI Service? Here's how: publish the same live report through the standard gateway, with nothing ClickHouse-specific installed on it. Disclosure: I'm the author of eMondrian, the open-source semantic layer used here. How it works: a semantic model in between eMondrian sits between Power BI and ClickHouse. It holds the model, with cubes, dimensions and measures such as On-Time Rate defined once. To Power BI it looks like Analysis Services.

articles.title: Agente de IA prepara, pessoa confirma: um modelo de design para apps que movem dinheiro
articles.excerpt: Quando um agente de IA pode agir sozinho e quando não pode? Em apps que movem dinheiro, uma regra simples ajuda muito: separe preparar de executar. O agente faz o trabalho pesado, e a pessoa decide. O…
articles.body: Quando um agente de IA pode agir sozinho e quando não pode? Em apps que movem dinheiro, uma regra simples ajuda muito: separe preparar de executar. O agente faz o trabalho pesado, e a pessoa decide. Preparar não é executar O agente pesquisa, monta a operação e mostra todos os parâmetros. Mas a execução só acontece depois de uma ação explícita de quem usa o app. Com isso, um erro do modelo vira um rascunho que a pessoa pode recusar, e não uma transação que já saiu. O que a tela de confirmação precisa mostrar Uma boa confirmação é legível em poucos segundos. Ela mostra o ativo, a rede, o valor, o destino e os custos estimados, e deixa claro o que é estimativa e o que é garantido. Evite jargão sem explicação, porque a pessoa precisa entender o que está aprovando.
articles.author: Jamie Parker

articles.excerpt: I’m Kaleb, running Dream Futures Tech right here in Pompano Beach, Florida. When local contractors around Palm Beach County—whether they are roofers in Boca Raton or plumbers in Fort Lauderdale—ask me…
articles.body: I’m Kaleb, running Dream Futures Tech right here in Pompano Beach, Florida. When local contractors around Palm Beach County—whether they are roofers in Boca Raton or plumbers in Fort Lauderdale—ask me why their website isn't turning traffic into phone calls, it usually comes down to friction. Either the contact form is buried, or their chat widget is completely broken by spam bots submitting fake leads every three seconds. I built a public chat and lead-capture endpoint on my own business website to test out automated SMS routing to my phone. It worked great until automated scrapers found the raw function URL. Suddenly, bots were hammering the endpoint fifty times a minute, trying to inject SQL strings and garbage URLs into my database.

articles.excerpt: The Market Is Changing Before We Have Learned How to Measure It For decades, businesses have competed for visibility. They competed for search rankings, advertising impressions, website traffic, brand…
articles.body: The Market Is Changing Before We Have Learned How to Measure It For decades, businesses have competed for visibility. They competed for search rankings, advertising impressions, website traffic, brand recognition, distribution channels, and ultimately market share. The measurement infrastructure was built around these activities. Search engines showed ranked results. Advertising platforms reported impressions and clicks. Analytics systems tracked visitors and conversions. Financial reports measured revenue and market position. But a new decision-making environment is emerging. A growing number of people are no longer beginning their purchasing journey by searching through ten blue links. Instead, they ask AI systems questions such as: Which software platform is best for my company?

articles.title: At 8 m, a rental wall is a sail before it is a screen
articles.excerpt: Every outdoor rental quote I get asked to review argues about pixel pitch and brightness. Almost none of them contains a wind number. Then the wall goes up 8 m tall on a plaza, the forecast turns, and…
articles.body: Every outdoor rental quote I get asked to review argues about pixel pitch and brightness. Almost none of them contains a wind number. Then the wall goes up 8 m tall on a plaza, the forecast turns, and at 2 a.m. the conversation is suddenly about sandbags. A rental wall is a sail that happens to emit light. The screen is the easy part. The rigging is where the money and the risk actually sit. What "6-level wind" means in newtons Beaufort 6 — strong breeze, the level where flags start snapping — is 10.8 to 13.8 m/s. Dynamic pressure is q = 0.613 × v², so that band is about 72 to 117 Pa. Multiply by a flat-plate drag coefficient of roughly 1.25 and take a 12 m × 8 m wall, 96 m² of sail: at 10.8 m/s: about 8.6 kN at 13.8 m/s: about 14 kN — 1.4 tonnes of horizontal push That is not a storm.

articles.title: Do we know how many Starship launches SpaceX will need to get NASA astronauts to the moon? No. Will its refuelling plan be simple? Also no.
articles.excerpt: NASA's Artemis IV moon mission will be a complicated affair — especially if SpaceX's Starship ends up being the lunar lander. The massive spacecraft will need an unknown number of refuel flights in tw…
articles.body: NASA's Artemis IV moon mission will be a complicated affair — especially if SpaceX's Starship ends up being the lunar lander. For all of the changing components of the Artemis program over the past several years, one of its most persistent may be the question of how many refueling flights Starship will need to land astronauts on the moon . By summer 2021, it was common knowledge that Starship would require multiple launches to pull off an Artemis moon landing. A Government Accountability Office audit at the time, for example, estimated that it could take up to 16. Earlier this month, a member of the Aerospace Safety Advisory Panel said the refueling number could be as high as 22.

articles.body: 6 Min Read Happy 65 Years: NASA’s Johnson Space Center Then and Now View of the Manned Spacecraft Center during construction in 1963. Sixty-five years ago, a bold vision took root in Houston: a NASA center dedicated to human spaceflight. Since its founding, NASA’s Johnson Space Center has helped lead the nation’s human spaceflight program, supporting missions from Project Mercury through Artemis. Today, Johnson serves as NASA’s Center of Excellence for Human Spaceflight, and its workforce is helping to usher in a Golden Age of innovation and discovery. Johnson is home to America’s astronaut corps, the Mission Control Center, and the teams behind some of humanity’s greatest achievements in space.
